title: Cash Discount and Payment-Term Claims
summary: Check every cash discount a dealer takes or claims against the invoice date, the payment date and your discount slabs, before the credit note goes out.

seo.title: Cash Discount Claims Reconciliation | VipraTech
seo.description: Validate cash discounts and prompt-payment claims against invoice dates, receipts, bounced cheques and your discount slabs before credit notes are raised.

designed_for: CFO or Head of Credit and Collections

problem.intro: Agri-input, building materials, chemicals, pharma and auto parts companies give dealers a cash discount for paying early, in slabs by the days taken to pay. Dealers either deduct it when they pay or claim it afterwards. With thousands of invoices, part payments, cheques that bounce and payments that cover several invoices, most companies check cash discounts in bulk and pay more than they owe.

pain_points.title: Discount taken on late payments
pain_points.detail: Payments made after the slab ends still get the higher discount, because receipts are not matched to invoices one by one.

pain_points.title: Bounced cheques keep the discount
pain_points.detail: The discount is given on the cheque date, and stays even when the cheque bounces and is paid late.

pain_points.title: Part payments and on-account receipts
pain_points.detail: Receipts that cover several invoices, or that arrive without references, are split by hand and often in the dealer's favour.

pain_points.title: Discount on the wrong value
pain_points.detail: Cash discount is calculated on the gross value instead of the value net of schemes, returns or taxes, as the policy says.

solution.overview: VipraTech matches each receipt to the invoices it settles, using references where they exist and your allocation rule, such as oldest invoice first, where they do not. It works out the days taken to pay each invoice from the date the money was actually realised, applies your slabs to the value the policy sets, and compares the result with the discount the dealer took or claimed. Bounced and re-presented cheques are followed through to the final realisation. Differences go to an exception queue, and finance approves the credit note or debit note sheet.
capabilities: Matches receipts to invoices, with your allocation rule for unreferenced payments
Counts days to pay from the realisation date, following bounced and re-presented cheques
Applies discount slabs by product group, region and dealer type
Calculates the discount on the value the policy sets, net of schemes and returns
Compares with the discount taken or claimed, and prepares credit or debit notes for the difference
Shows days to pay and discount cost by dealer and region

workflow.title: Load receivables
workflow.detail: Invoices, receipts, bank realisation dates and cheque returns are loaded for the period.

workflow.title: Allocate receipts
workflow.detail: Each receipt is allocated to invoices by reference or by your allocation rule.

workflow.title: Count days to pay
workflow.detail: Days to pay are counted from invoice or due date to realisation, per invoice.

workflow.title: Apply slabs
workflow.detail: Your discount slabs are applied to the eligible value of each invoice.

workflow.title: Compare and review
workflow.detail: Calculated discount is compared with what was taken or claimed, and differences go to review.

workflow.title: Settle
workflow.detail: Finance approves credit notes for discount due and debit notes for discount taken wrongly.

match_rules.logic: Each receipt is allocated by invoice reference. Without one, your rule applies, such as oldest invoice first.
Days to pay run from the invoice or due date to the date the money was realised in your bank, not the cheque date.
A returned cheque cancels the discount until the amount is realised again, and the new date sets the slab.

match_rules.rule: Slab for the dealer and product
match_rules.logic: Slabs are chosen by product group, region and dealer type from the policy version in force on the invoice date.
The discount is calculated on the value the policy sets, such as net of schemes, returns or taxes.

exception_codes.meaning: The discount taken is for a faster slab than the days to pay allow.
exception_codes.action: Raise a debit note for the difference.

exception_codes.meaning: The cheque bounced, so the discount was not earned on its date.
exception_codes.action: Recalculate from the final realisation date.

exception_codes.meaning: A receipt could not be allocated with confidence.
The discount was calculated on the wrong value.
The dealer earned a discount that was not given.

inputs: Sales invoices with dates, due dates and values
Receipts with mode, reference and amount
Bank statements with realisation dates and cheque returns
Scheme and return credit notes for the eligible value
outputs: Discount due per invoice beside discount taken
Credit and debit note sheet for finance approval
Exceptions with reason codes and bank evidence
Days to pay and discount cost by dealer and region
human_in_the_loop: The credit team decides every unallocated receipt and every recovery from a dealer. Finance approves all credit and debit notes.
integrations: ERP such as SAP or Tally for invoices, receipts and notes
Bank statements by download or feed
Shared drive for the discount policy
guardrails: Days counted from realisation, never from cheque date alone
Policy version applied by invoice date
Unallocated receipts never guessed: they go to a person
Every difference shown with the receipt and bank line
compliance_notes: Cash discount passed through credit notes may need the original invoice reference for GST; the system keeps it.

rollout.scope: One quarter of invoices and receipts for one region, compared with the discounts finance allowed.
deliverables: Discount policy set up as rules

what_we_measure.how: Share of receipts allocated to invoices without manual work.
Discount taken above what the days to pay allow.
Discount dealers earned but were not given.

faqs.q: Our dealers pay against several invoices at once. Can it allocate?
faqs.a: Yes. It uses invoice references where they exist and your rule, such as oldest invoice first, where they do not. Receipts it cannot allocate with confidence go to your team.

faqs.q: Can it handle different slabs for different products?
faqs.a: Yes. Slabs are set by product group, region and dealer type, and each invoice uses the slab in force on its date.
Days to pay count to the date the money is realised, so a post-dated cheque earns the slab for its realisation date.

faqs.q: Will dealers see why a discount was reduced?
faqs.a: Yes. Each dealer statement shows the invoice, the receipt, the days to pay and the slab applied.
